text:
maya: flagging a perf regression after the latest kernel selector patch. host-side parse+tokenize p95 up ~30% on ingress canary.

joel: any flame or counters? is it parse CPU or more syscalls from streaming?
 maya: short profile:
```
CPU 70s
  tokenizer/ingress.go:scan     18s (26%)
  parser/frame.go:frameParse    10s (14%)
  grpc/writer.go:sysFlush       7s  (10%)
  selector/choose.go:score      2s  (3%)
```

frank: selector scoring low time but did it pick much smaller kernels more often? that can make the host emit more tiny chunks.

maya: selector breakdown: small-variant 5% -> 45% in canary. tcp write size p95 moved from 520B -> 190B; small-write count tripled.

cassie: small frames explain syscall pressure + parse overhead. what's the canary config? minibatch_ms? kernel flags?
 maya: config excerpt: minibatch_timeout_ms=2, minibatch_size=4, selector_bias=latency_small=true.

joel: mitigation plan: revert the selector_bias flag in canary, bump minibatch_timeout to 6ms, and add a soft-coalesce in grpc writer (threshold 512B).

infra-bot: deploy-canary cassie/revert-small-bias -> ingress-canary-4 started at 1799999120 :rocket:

maya: 11m after revert: tokenize+parse CPU -24%, small writes -61%, kv hit-rate returned. tail latency unchanged.

frank: follow-ups: (1) add unit test simulating stream-fragmentation with forced small variants, (2) emit metrics parse_bytes_per_request and grpc_coalesce_misses/s, (3) prototype selector cost term for expected_host_writes.

cassie: I'll PR the writer coalesce and add config flag. joel can you instrument selector to report expected write ops per choice?

joel: on it. also filing INF-4999 to track selector-host IO integration.

infra-bot: canary completed at 1799999400 ✅ 3/3 healthy.

maya: good catch. adding "simulate streaming workload" to kernel-change checklist so future selector tweaks run this scenario in the perf harness.

frank: agree. these cross-layer effects are subtle — kernel-only perf numbers miss host framing costs.

cassie: PRs incoming, will link benchmarks when ready.
